Azerbaijani

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

сука (definite accusative суканы, plural сукалар)

  1. Cyrillic spelling of suka

[edit]

nominative сука сукалар
definite accusative суканы сукалары
dative сукаја сукалара

ablative сукадан сукалардан
definite genitive суканын сукаларын

Komi-Permyak

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From сук (suk, “dense”) +‎ -а (-a).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈsuka/, [ˈsukä]
  • Hyphenation: сук‧а

Adjective

[edit]

су́ка • (súka)

  1. dense, thick
    Synonym: тшӧк (čök)

Macedonian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈsuka]
  • Rhymes: -uka

Verb

[edit]

сука • (suka) third-singular present, impf (perfective исука or засука)

  1. (transitive) to flatten with a rolling pin
  2. (transitive) to roll up (e.g. sleeves)
  3. (transitive) to twirl (moustache)

Old East Slavic

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *sùka, further etymology unclear.

Noun

[edit]

су́ка (súka) f

  1. bitch (female dog)
  2. (vulgar, offensive) bitch

Descendants

[edit]
  • Old Ruthenian: *сука (*suka)
    • Belarusian: су́ка́ (súká)
    • Carpathian Rusyn: су́ка (súka)
    • Ukrainian: су́ка (súka); су́ля (súlja)
  • Russian: су́ка (súka)

[edit]

(1912), “сꙋка”, in Матеріалы для Словаря древне-русскаго языка по письменнымъ памятникамъ [Materials for the Dictionary of the Old East Slavic Language Based on Written Monuments]‎[2] (in Russian), volume 3 (Р – Ꙗ и дополненія), Saint Petersburg: Department of Russian Language and Literature of the Imperial Academy of Sciences, column 614
  • Krysko, V. B., editor (2019), “соука”, in Словарь древнерусского языка (XI–XIV вв.) [Dictionary of the Old Russian Language (11ᵗʰ–14ᵗʰ cc.)] (in Russian), volume 12 (соу – съотъходьнъ), Moscow: Azbukovnik, →ISBN, page 63
  • Krysko, V. B., editor (2008), “сука”, in Словарь русского языка XI–XVII вв. [Dictionary of the Russian Language: 11ᵗʰ–17ᵗʰ cc.] (in Russian), issue 28 (старичекъ – сулебный), Moscow: Nauka, →ISBN, page 285

Pannonian Rusyn

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈsuka]
  • Rhymes: -uka
  • Hyphenation: су‧ка

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Old Slovak suka, from Proto-Slavic *suka. Cognates include Carpathian Rusyn су́ка (súka) and Slovak suka.

Noun

[edit]

сука (suka) f (relational adjective суков or сучи)

  1. bitch (female dog)
  2. (vulgar, derogatory) bitch, slut, prostitute
    Synonyms: гойда (hojda), гонюха (honjuxa), (obsolete) флюндра (fljundra)
    Near-synonym: курва (kurva)
Declension
[edit]

nominative сука (suka) суки (suki)
genitive суки (suki) сукох (sukox)

accusative суку (suku) суки (suki)
instrumental суку (suku) суками (sukami)
locative суки (suki) сукох (sukox)
vocative суко (suko) суки (suki)

[edit]

  • Fejsa, M.; Šlemender, M.; Čelʹovski, S. (2022), “bitch”, in Анґлийско-руски словнїк [English-Rusyn Dictionary] (in Pannonian Rusyn), Novi Sad: Faculty of Philosophy; Ruska matka, →ISBN, page 38

[edit]

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Verb

[edit]

сука (suka)

  1. third-person singular indicative present of сукац (sukac)

Russian

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Old East Slavic сука (suka), from Proto-Slavic *sùka, further etymology unclear. Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *ḱwṓ.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈsukə]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

су́ка • (súka) f anim (genitive су́ки, nominative plural су́ки, genitive plural сук, relational adjective су́чий, possessive adjective су́кин, diminutive су́чка, augmentative суча́ра)

  1. bitch (female dog)
  2. (vulgar, offensive) bitch (contemptible person, usually but not necessarily female)
  3. (vulgar, offensive) frivolous, promiscuous female
  4. (vulgar, offensive, slang) sometimes used to denote any female
  5. (prison slang) snitch, inmate who collaborates with prison administration

Interjection

[edit]

су́ка • (súka)

  1. (vulgar, swear word) shit!, fuck!
    • 2023 May 5, Yevgeny Prigozhin, as quoted, “«Шойгу, Герасимов, где, сука, боеприпасы?» Пригожин записал видео для Минобороны на фоне трупов наемников ЧВК Вагнера (много мата)”, in Meduza‎[3]:
      Шойгу, Герасимов, где, сука, боеприпасы?
      Šojgu, Gerasimov, gde, suka, bojepripasy?
      Shoigu, Gerasimov, where is the fucking ammunition?

Ukrainian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • су ка (su ka) (online slang, interjection)
  • сук (suk) (online slang, interjection)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old East Slavic сука (suka), from Proto-Slavic *sùka, further etymology unclear.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈsukɐ]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

су́ка • (súka) f inan (genitive су́ки, nominative plural су́ки, genitive plural сук, relational adjective су́чий)

  1. (vulgar) bitch, fucker
  2. bitch, female dog
